title: Pullback, tensor product and direct images on $\Dctf$ at all coefficient stages
statement:
Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\Zl,\mathcal O_E,\Ql,E,\Qlb\}$ be admissible and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type of the standing schemes.

1. $f^*$ maps $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$, and
   $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_\Lambda$ maps $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)\times\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$
   into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.
2. For a locally closed immersion $a$ (in particular a quasi-compact open
   immersion), $a_!$ preserves $\Dctf$.
3. $Rf_*$ and $Rf_!$ map $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$.
4. $f^!$ maps $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Use the admissible rings of [sk-def-localizing-closure], including every finite commutative $\ell$-primary ring $A$, and the arbitrary characteristic-$p$ field setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. All schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. They are therefore qcqs, and every open subset is quasi-compact. By [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback], the exact inverse image $f^*$ preserves $\Dctf$ for every admissible coefficient. This proves the pullback assertion. For integral and rational coefficients, [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] gives $\Dctf=\Dbc$; this equality will never be used for an arbitrary finite ring $A$.

For finite $A$, descend $K,L\in\Dctf(X,A)$ to the étale site by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]; $A$ is Noetherian because every ideal is a finite set. Choose ordered Tor intervals $[a,b]$, $[c,d]$. By [lem-sf-etale-flat-constructible], represent the descended objects by bounded complexes $P,Q$ of flat constructible sheaves, zero outside these intervals. Refine the finitely many stratifications of their terms by [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-stratification-intersection]. On each stratum, [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-tensor], applied to the flat terms in degree zero, shows that $P^i\otimes_AQ^j$ is locally constant of finite type. Finite sums and the kernels and cokernels computing cohomology are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. Each tensor term is flat: tensoring with $P^i\otimes_AQ^j$ is the composite of two exact tensor functors; finite sums remain exact. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_AQ)$ is a bounded flat complex, supported in $[a+c,b+d]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site], so it computes the derived tensor and has this Tor interval against every module sheaf. The monoidal comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identifies its exact pro-étale pullback with $K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L$. The Tor comparison equivalence gives the finite-coefficient tensor assertion of (1).

proof.text: Let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion. Since the schemes are Noetherian, it is quasi-compact; [lem-pqf-qc-immersion-open-closed-factor] factors it as $S\xrightarrow{u}T\xrightarrow{i}X$ with $u$ open and $i$ closed. The coefficient sheaves are cartesian by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to the pairs $(T,S)$ and $(X,X\setminus T)$: $u_!$ and $i_*$ are exact, their restriction back to their support is the identity, and their restrictions to the respective complements are zero. Hence $a_!=i_*u_!$ is exact and acts termwise on the derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. If $F$ is constructible on $S$, take its finite stratification from [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. The stratum immersions composed with $a$ are immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Together with $T\setminus S$ and $X\setminus T$ these give a finite locally closed stratification of $X$; all its strata are constructible because $X$ is Noetherian. On the source strata the restriction of $a_!F$ is the given finite constant local model, and on the two complementary strata it is zero, by the restriction identities just cited. Therefore $a_!F$ is constructible. For $K\in\Dctf(S,\Lambda)$, exactness gives $H^n(a_!K)=a_!H^n(K)$, so $a_!K$ is bounded constructible. If $K$ has Tor interval $[a_0,b_0]$, then for every target module sheaf $N$, [det-lem-int-tensor-projection] gives $(a_!K)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_X}N\simeq a_!(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_S}a^*N)$. The pullback $a^*N$ is a sheaf by cartesian coefficients, and exact $a_!$ preserves vanishing outside $[a_0,b_0]$. Thus $a_!K$ has the same Tor interval. This proves (2) uniformly for every admissible coefficient, without replacing $K$ by its cohomology for the Tor test.

proof.text: Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be open and $A$ finite. Descend $K\in\Dctf(U,A)$ of Tor interval $[a,b]$ to an étale complex $C$ by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. Its étale direct image $B=Rj_*C$ is bounded constructible by [cor-fin-deligne-open-finite-coefficients], since a power of $\ell$ kills $A$ and is invertible in $k$. Put $d=\operatorname{cd}(j)<\infty$ by [lem-kun-0f10](1). Clause (1) of [det-geo-open-finiteness-ii-amplitude] states $R^qj_*F=0$ for all sheaves $F$ and $q>d$. Consequently $Rj_*$ maps any étale complex with cohomology in $[a,b]$ into degrees $[a,b+d]$: its finite truncation filtration has factors $H^r[-r]$ for $a\le r\le b$, each of whose direct images lies in $[r,r+d]$, and the long exact cohomology sequences retain the common bound. For every finitely presented $A$-module $M$, [lem-sf-projection-finite-constant] identifies $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_X$ with $Rj_*(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M_U)$, hence bounds it in $[a,b+d]$. Now take any geometric point $x$ of $X$. Stalks are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], and their derived tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], so $B_x\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M$ has that bound. Every $A$-module $V$ is the filtered union of its finitely generated submodules; these are finite sets, hence finitely presented over the finite ring $A$. Resolve $B_x$ by a K-flat complex with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-point ringed site. Tensor commutes with this filtered union termwise, and exact filtered colimits of modules, supplied by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] on that site, commute with cohomology. It follows that $B_x\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}V$ has the same bound for arbitrary $V$. For any module sheaf $N$ on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$, apply this with $V=N_x$. Exact conservative geometric stalks [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] detect vanishing of $B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N$, so $B$ has Tor interval $[a,b+d]$ on the étale site. Finally [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] identifies $\nu_X^*B$ with the pro-étale $Rj_*K$, and [lem-exc-comparison-tor-interval] transfers the bound against every pro-étale module sheaf. This proves the finite open direct-image case over the arbitrary standing field.

proof.text: For $\mathcal O_E$ and a quasi-compact open immersion $j$, [det-thm-sf-pf-adic-open] gives $Rj_*:\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)\to\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, including derived completeness and the reduction comparison. Step 1 translates this to preservation of $\Dctf$.

The coefficient categories in this step are compared by exact conservative restriction of scalars, which leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Exactness follows because kernels and cokernels have the restricted action on the same underlying sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], derived restriction is termwise restriction. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to the commuting square of $j$ and the identity-topos ring morphisms defining scalar restriction: $\operatorname{Res}Rj_*^{\Lambda'}\simeq Rj_*^\Lambda\operatorname{Res}$. Thus continuity computed after scalar restriction computes the actual direct image in the larger coefficient category. For rational coefficients it suffices to check the generators of [det-lem-integral-models-generators], since $Rj_*$ is triangulated and the rational categories $\Dbc$ are closed under finite cones and shifts by [det-cor-coefficient-heart-ii-triangulated]. Write an $E$-generator as $M[1/\ell]$, where $M=a_!L_0$ is an integral constructible sheaf. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], localization is the filtered system $M\xrightarrow{\ell}M\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots$, all in degree zero. Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] to this diagram: its cohomology comparisons, and exact filtered colimits of module sheaves from [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], show that the canonical map $(Rj_*M)[1/\ell]\to Rj_*(M[1/\ell])$ is a quasi-isomorphism after restriction of scalars, hence an isomorphism. By Step 6, $Rj_*M$ is bounded constructible. Localization is flat by [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell]; it preserves its cohomology interval and extends the finite constant local presentations of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] on the same finite strata to presentations over $E$. Thus this image is in $\Dbc(X,E)$. For a $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-generator, [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] expresses scalar extension as the filtered colimit over finite $F/E$. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], each $F_X$ is finite free over $E_X$, and so $Rj_*$ commutes with scalar extension to $F$ by additivity, after choosing an $E$-basis. The diagram $F_U\otimes_{E_U}M[1/\ell]$ again consists of sheaves in degree zero. Bounded continuity therefore gives $Rj_*(\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,U}\otimes_{E_U}M[1/\ell])\simeq\overline{\mathbf Q}_{\ell,X}\otimes_{E_X}Rj_*(M[1/\ell])$. This filtered scalar extension is flat: tensoring is the filtered colimit of the exact finite-free tensor functors, and filtered colimits are exact. It preserves the bounded cohomology interval and extends the finite constant local presentations to ones over $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Hence the image is bounded constructible. Finite cones and shifts conclude both rational open cases, and Step 1 translates them to $\Dctf$.

proof.text: For proper $p$, finite-coefficient preservation is [det-ctf-finite-proper-localizing](1), for every finite $\ell$-primary ring $A$. For $\mathcal O_E$ it is the constructibility conclusion of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral](1); for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ it is [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational](2). Step 1 translates the integral and rational $\Dbc$ conclusions to $\Dctf$. Thus proper direct image preserves $\Dctf$ at every coefficient stage.

source.place: paragraph 2, proper direct image at all coefficient stages

proof.text: Choose the compactification $f=pj$ supplied by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], whose intermediate scheme is again in the standing setting. The derived direct-image composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied to the cartesian coefficient sheaves of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], gives $Rf_*\simeq Rp_*Rj_*$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek], the specified compactly supported image is $Rf_!=Rp_*D(j_!)$, where $j_!$ is exact. Steps 5--8 show that the first composite preserves $\Dctf$, and Steps 4 and 8 show this for the second. This proves (3) for the specified ambient derived functors and compactification.

For (4), apply the restriction assertion of [sk-prop-sf-rf-shriek-preservation] for every finite admissible $A$, [sk-thm-int-restriction] for $\mathcal O_E$, and [sk-thm-restriction] for $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Each statement explicitly sends $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$ into $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ for the exceptional right adjoint; existence on a localizing closure alone is not used as preservation. Taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ covers $\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $\mathbf Q_\ell$. These conclusions and Steps 1--9 give all four clauses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NL-5551fb7b8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all ten steps and the statements of all 46 cited nodes against the main-20261015 source and the units; the delivery adds no new nodes. The statement is verbatim and no target is weakened. Steps 1-3: pullback for every admissible ring comes from det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback. For finite A, tensor uses the etale flat constructible model, the common refinement of strata, 094H on flat degree-0 terms and K-flatness by 06YQ, giving the interval [a+c,b+d]; this moves to pro-etale by the 07A4 pullback and the Noetherian Tor-comparison equivalence. Dctf=Dbc is used only for the integral and rational rings. Step 4: a_! uses the 01QV factorization, exactness from the open/closed lemma, an explicit stratification and det-lem-int-tensor-projection tested against every sheaf N, so the whole complex is tested; this is correct for nonregular A. Step 5 is needed because cor-sf-direct-image-ctf-proetale covers only k=Fbar_q and A_{E,n}. Its inputs check out: finite open direct image over any field, relative cd from Stacks 0F10(1) (checked in the .tex), uniform vanishing, the finitely presented projection formula, and an arbitrary-module stalk test with K-flat resolutions and filtered colimits, then the comparison isomorphism and Tor transfer. Steps 6-7 follow the route of sk-prop-open-coefficients: integral open preservation, then integral generators, bounded continuity on degree-0 colimits after restriction of scalars (0D6E), flat localization and finite-free extensions. Step 8 checks the finite, integral (1) and rational (2) proper results. Step 9 uses the chosen compactification, Rf_*=Rp_*Rj_*, and Rf_!=Rp_*D(j_!). Step 10 uses the three restriction theorems; the f^! of det-prop-int-brown-adjoint is stated to be that of sk-prop-sf-existence. Edge cases tested: zero objects, empty schemes, identity immersions, A=Z/l^2 and infinite cd(k). All 15 Stacks tags match their labels. There is no cycle, no merged citation, no duplicate and no SGA citation. I accept the declared tool_uses. The unit record sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability is the stale master unit, and lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site should cite 06YQ, not 06YS; both are maintainer metadata, not faults of this delivery. No fixes.
